questions.prompt: What's the key difference between Claude Code and a chat assistant?

options.text: Claude Code uses a smarter model
Claude Code can act — read files, edit them, and run commands — not just produce text for you to act on
Claude Code can't hold a conversation

questions.explanation: Same kind of model underneath — the difference is hands. Chat gives you advice to carry out yourself; Claude Code carries it out in a real folder while you direct. It converses fine (c), and chat assistants write code too — they just can't run or save it (d).

questions.prompt: Put the agent loop in order: which step comes right after Claude takes an action (like running a command)?

options.text: It observes the result of that action and uses it to decide what to do next
It immediately declares the task done
It forgets the action and starts over
It waits for you to describe what happened

questions.explanation: Observe is the step that makes it an agent: the actual output of the command flows back into the loop, so mistakes get caught and corrected. It doesn't declare victory blind (b) or need you to relay results (d) — seeing outcomes for itself is the whole point.

questions.prompt: Why do your prompting skills from earlier modules still matter with Claude Code?

options.text: They don't — agents ignore how you phrase things
The goal you give in plain English is still a prompt: specific goals with clear context and constraints steer the whole loop
Prompts only matter for the first message
Claude Code requires prompts written in code

questions.explanation: Everything you learned — be specific, give context, state the format of 'done' — now steers an agent instead of a single reply, which makes it MORE valuable, not less. Vague goal, wandering agent. And no, you direct it in ordinary English, not code (d).
